description: Understand your project: problems, rules and a code map. No AI.
view.welcome:
Open a folder to analyze it.
[Analyze project](command:spectator.scan)
cfg.scanOnSave: Analyze again when a file is saved.
cfg.diagnostics: Show problems underlined in the editor.
cfg.maxFiles: Maximum number of files to analyze.
cfg.language: Language of Spectator. "auto" follows the VS Code display language.
wt.title: Get started with Spectator
wt.desc: Five steps to know what to review in your project.
wt.analizar.title: Analyze your project
wt.analizar.desc:
Spectator reads your code without running it and looks for problems.
[Analyze project](command:spectator.scan)
wt.resumen.title: See your next step
wt.resumen.desc:
The panel tells you what to review first. Press "Technical details" only if you want more information.
[Open the panel](command:spectator.open)
wt.reglas.title: Confirm your rules
wt.reglas.desc:
Mark important limits and values as correct. If someone changes them, I will tell you.
[See the rules](command:spectator.open?%5B%7B%22tab%22%3A%22statements%22%7D%5D)
wt.vivo.title: Watch your program run (Node.js)
wt.vivo.desc:
Run a command and see which functions are really used. Running it also runs your project code.
[Watch live](command:spectator.trace)
cmd.activity: Spectator: Show activity (changes, API and logs)
cmd.watchLogs: Spectator: Read errors from a log file
cfg.apiTarget: URL of your server for the API watcher (for example http://localhost:8080). Empty: guessed from the project and asked.
cfg.apiPort: Local port of the API watcher. Call your API through it. 0 = any free port.
cfg.mode: How Spectator is presented: simple (the essentials and the next step) or professional (all technical data visible).
wt.api.title: Work alongside IntelliJ and watch your API
wt.api.desc:
Open the same folder you have in IntelliJ: Spectator will see every change. To understand your API errors (500, 404…), watch it and call it through the address it gives you.
[Watch the API](command:spectator.watchApi)
cmd.live: Spectator: Run the app and test its API (Spring Boot, Node/Express)
cfg.live.allowWrites: Live mode may send POST and PUT requests even when the database is not in memory. Enable only for test databases.
cfg.live.restartOnSave: Restart the app run by live mode and repeat its API tests when you save Java code or configuration.
cfg.aiLogs: Read the local Claude Code and Codex logs to know which AI changed each file. Only paths, times and the changed snippet are read; never the conversations.
cfg.followActiveFolder: With several workspace folders, switch to the folder of the file you open.
